reviews.comment: Great lecturer though expect less flexibility about her expectations for you. She expects timeliness and hard work, but you will learn a lot if you buy in.

Much worse than lectures. Simple questions are often treated as misunderstandings, with limited patience. Guidance for first-time researchers is minimal, with many expectations assumed rather than explained. Heavy emphasis on results, with little consideration of overall course load. Avoid is possible.

The professor was a very principled educator to be frank. She lectures well, and gives a lot of great study material if you fill in the problems during class, but exams are hard and not enough time is given. Be sure to have a near 100% attendance, and she will curve you out of an F or D to a C. Weekly quizzes, hard exams.

Completely unreasonable professor. Locks the doors to the lectures if you're a literal minute late acting like we don't pay thousands to take the class. Why would you become a professor if you don't like seeing students succeed? DO NOT TAKE

Dr. Wright is an amazing prof. Yes she is blunt and rude at times, but she clearly cares for students. Her lectures are in depth and very effective. She runs a tight ship, do not miss a class unless needed. Her exams are very fast so prepare well. Her office hours are great for clarifying stuff. Heat transfer is difficult, she is the best there is.

She can not be flexible whatsoever. If you're sick for a quiz, she will not let you retake it, you simply get a 0 on it whether it's excused or not. If you miss an exam she will simply make your final be worth 50% of your total grade. I have nothing but bad things to say about this experience. Worst I have had in my MEEN coursework.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attitude problem. She has constant power trip when it comes to the most simplest questions. I don't know what her deal is, but I guarantee she has a plaque at home that says, "my way or the highway". I will say she is great at teaching the material. Had MWF lecture and exams were only 50 mins long, don't know many people that finished them.

I came out of MEEN 461 hardly needing to read the textbook. I credit that to Dr. Wright's lecture style and teaching. She and Dr. Cope are tied for best MEEN professor in my opinion (different styles but both teach material effectively).

The grading for this class is much more difficult than fluids. But if you want to learn I'd take Dr. Wright.

Professor Wright is incredibly strict with timeliness, and her grading can be brutal at times. The tests are definitely a time crunch, but if you attend the lectures and complete the homework, they aren't too terribly difficult. Above all, she is very knowledgeable and a wonderful lecturer. I learned a lot from her class.

The format of the class is pretty standard with homeworks, quizzes, exams. Her grading can be questionable at times and rarely will help you out, and the same goes for missing class. She's quite a stickler with attendance and won't take anything that is not university excused as an excuse. She is good at teaching, but not very understanding w life

461 is a tough class but Dr. Wright is a really good and inspiring lecturer. She is great at explaining/breaking things down. Definitely runs a tight ship so don't be late. Quizzes/exams were a time crunch but aligned reasonably with the lecture problems and homework. Found it very helpful to independently rework problems solved in class.

This class is a lot of work regardless of prof due to lab reports, it is all dependent on studio TA. However, the final in the class, while painful, is worth very little of your entire grade. Additionally, she is the only prof to not give quizzes in lecture. There are very few homeworks and attendance is for extra credit.

Dr. Wright was a great lecturer, very nice and esay to reach out to. Had difficulties understanding the material and she patiently explain them every time I go to office hour. She made sure we understand the material. The grading was a bit harsh but very reasonable.

Ridicules you for the questions you have and grades ridiculously harsh. She will say things like "if I dont trust you with my life I cannot give you an A" and then not emphasize the things she deems life-saving which is hilariously stupid. Should have got an A but she was NOT having it.

Good teacher. Class was taught in such a way that you could watch the lectures live or as recorded videos. Overall, professor was very clear on the requirements for the homework and projects. Lectures were relatively entertaining. Course material was well-paced. The one negative for me is that the Professor wasn't very accessible outside of class.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Wright is extremely rude (she will not answer your questions in class and makes you feel bad for even asking a question) and is an incredibly tough grader. She will take off points for even the smallest reason.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: At the beginning of the semester, her great lectures and examples made me think that this class would be great. After finding out how insanely tough she is on grading made me scared if I'd even pass the class. The only way I did pass was because of the group projects. DO NOT TAKE

Probably the most unreasonable grader I have ever seen. When working out a problem I lost a significant number of points for writing an equation and didn't use it later and for not printing out the problems. There's also no chance of her curving your class she's a very cold professor.

Great lecturer and example solver, absolutely terrible at anything else. Grades absurdly hard for a class that requires lots of assumptions. Good luck asking questions outside of class, she is almost demeaning in her answers and feedback. Seems as if she enjoys lecturing but hates actually helping students. Do not take if possible.

I did not have a good experience with this professor. Would often respond to emails with biting remarks. Probably the harshest grader I have had in college. Lots of homework, discussion boards, projects, and lecture videos.

She is a decent lady and nice during lecture, but her tough grading on exams and homeworks make this class unpleasant. While she does goes over examples during lecture, the problems on the homework tend to be harder and much more complex than the in class examples. The weekly forum posts are also annoying

Dr. Wright makes good notes, explains concepts, and works out problems well, but she is unnecessarily tough when it comes to grading. Heat transfer is a hard class in general but she takes off points for silly things, such as submitting an assignment twice. It is also often discouraging to ask for help. Would rather have had a different prof.

I felt like she did a good job with what she was given. Lectures were always recorded and uploaded at a reasonable time. They were super thorough. Lots of homework in addition to discussion board questions and projects. Feedback on these assignments were not always helpful. I felt like I was being ridiculed sometimes for my questions I would ask.

Watching lectures will prepare you for all you need to know in her class. She grades very hard on homeworks and tests and does not offer much partial credit - things must be done as she teaches in her lecture videos with no deviance. She is very caring over her videos and in class, but reaching out to her outside is difficult and almost discouraged

Great lecturer. Teaches very well. Homework was graded exceptionally hard. Super nice and sweet during class, but outside of class she is sort of different. I went to her office hours a couple of times and felt like she did not want me there - her answers were very vague and short. But other than that, she is a great professor.
